_comment: Tier-2: Kratos requires element names with explicit node count (e.g. SmallDisplacementElement2D4N, not SmallDisplacement2D). The pitfall (kratos.linear_elasticity #0 from the existing catalog): 'Element names MUST include node count'. Verified operationally: CreateNewElement('SmallDisplacement2D', ...) raises RuntimeError 'Element ... is not registered'. MUTATION CONTROL (added 2026-08-06, re-runnable) -- THIS MUTATION DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. T2_MUTATE=1 replaces the suffix-less 'SmallDisplacement2D' with the correctly suffixed, genuinely registered name 'SmallDisplacementElement2D4N'. The fixture STAYS GREEN: it still raises RuntimeError ... "SmallDisplacementElement2D4N" is not registered! Reason, probed directly on this build: this fixture imports only core KratosMultiphysics and never imports StructuralMechanicsApplication, so NO structural element is registered at all. Measured with CreateNewElement on a 4-node quad: core-only SmallDisplacement2D creatable=False, core-only SmallDisplacementElement2D4N creatable=False; after 'import KratosMultiphysics.StructuralMechanicsApplication', SmallDisplacement2D creatable=False, SmallDisplacementElement2D4N creatable=True. So the expect strings 'RuntimeError' and 'not registered' select 'some element name is unregistered in a bare core model part', NOT the claim the fixture makes, which is that a name lacking the node-count suffix is rejected. Kratos's own message says as much: 'Maybe you need to import the application where it is defined?'. A correctly-named element fails this fixture identically to a wrongly-named one, so the fixture cannot fail for the reason it claims to test. The hook is left in place unadjusted so the defect stays re-runnable; per the campaign rule the mutation was NOT tuned until it passed. FIX (not applied here, out of scope): import StructuralMechanicsApplication in the fixture and add 'SmallDisplacement2D' to expect_in_output so the message is tied to the wrong name specifically. Re-verify: cd scripts/tier2_fixtures/kratos/element_name_missing_node_count && /usr/bin/python3 source.py (passes), then T2_MUTATE=1 /usr/bin/python3 source.py (STILL passes -- that is the defect). Interpreter: KRATOS_PYTHON=/usr/bin/python3 is REQUIRED on this host -- the repo venv Kratos wheel is built against GLIBC_2.32 and fails to load (ImportError on Kratos.cpython-312...so), while the system python3.8 carries Kratos 10.4 Release with CableNet, ConstitutiveLaws, StructuralMechanics and LinearSolvers.
